pull.title: KAFKA-21111 [1/N]: Tell the refiner which members may be given a warm-up task
pull.body:
This is the first change of a series that makes the warm-up task refiner
(KAFKA-20665) compatible with clients that speak version 0 of the
streams group heartbeat (4.2 and 4.3), and with a coordinator failover
during which the coordinator does not know the version of any member. A
warm-up task is only useful if the coordinator can observe how far its
holder has restored it, which a member reports through the task offsets
of a version 1 heartbeat. A version 0 member never does, so it could
never be promoted from warm-up to active.

This change only provides the information, and nothing uses it yet. The
coordinator records the version of every member's last heartbeat as
transient state of the streams group, with the same lifecycle as the
reported task offsets: written in the heartbeat path, dropped when the
member is removed, and not known again after a coordinator failover
until the member heartbeats. It is deliberately not persisted, so that
it can never outlive the client that sent it. The refiner is handed an
immutable view of it, and decides itself which versions it can warm up.
A member that is missing from the map, because the coordinator has not
heard from the member since it loaded the group, has an unknown version.
The refiner ignores the new input for now; the following changes of this
series use it.

See https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-21111. The tests cover
the group state and the versions reaching the refiner through the
heartbeat path.

Reviewers: Bill Bejeck <bbejeck@apache.org>

review_comments.body: This validation is bypassed when an intermediate assignment is already cached: `refinedAssignmentForEpoch` returns the cached value at lines 4761–4764 without calling this method. After a failover, an UNKNOWN member may legitimately keep a cached warm-up; if that member then heartbeats with version 0 while the group is still RECONCILING, the coordinator reuses the cache and continues reconciling the unsupported member toward that warm-up instead of falling back to the target assignment. Revalidate cached assignments against the current support map (and replace/evict the cache on failure), or invalidate the cache when support becomes NOT_SUPPORTED.

This only emits support for members already replayed into `members`, but the heartbeat path calls `updateHeartbeatVersion` before a joining member's metadata record is replayed. During a join or static-member replacement, the just-observed v1 member is therefore omitted and treated as UNKNOWN by both the refiner contract and the guard, causing a valid warm-up placement for that newcomer to be discarded. Include recorded-but-not-yet-replayed members, or derive support from the same pending membership view used for target assignment.

review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -69,6 +72,10 @@ public interface AssignmentRefiner {
      *        The latest changelog offsets/end-offsets reported by the members via heartbeats, from which the lag
      *        of a warm-up task is derived. Not populated for a member that has not reported any offsets yet, for
      *        example right after a coordinator failover.
+     * @param warmupSupport
+     *        Whether each member may be handed a warm-up task, keyed by member ID. A member that is missing from the
+     *        map is {@link WarmupSupport#UNKNOWN}. The refiner never places a warm-up task on a member that is not
+     *        {@link WarmupSupport#SUPPORTED}, except that it keeps one that a member of unknown version already holds.
review_comments.body: This states that the refiner enforces the restriction, but `AssignmentRefinerImpl` intentionally does not use this parameter in this change; enforcement currently happens in the coordinator after `refine` returns. Document the coordinator-side validation instead so implementers do not rely on a guarantee the built-in implementation does not provide.

Imports in this group are lexicographically ordered (as the adjacent `TasksTuple` and `TopologyMetadata` imports show), but `WarmupSupport` is inserted before `TopologyMetadata`. Swap these imports to satisfy the enforced import-order formatting.

A cached intermediate assignment was validated when it was derived, and I don't see a path where a member's support changes afterwards. A member ID belongs to one client instance, and a restart gets a new member ID, so an UNKNOWN member can only hold a cached warm-up if it is a version 1 client that held it before the failover. Revalidating on every heartbeat would also add an O(members) pass to each heartbeat of a reconciling group. Happy to add it if you see a way a member's version can change under the same member ID.

The refiner is handed `group.members()` as well, which is the group state without a member whose join record has not been replayed yet, so `warmupSupport()` and the refiner see the same membership. A joining member is not in the refiner's input either, and its target tasks are parked on their old owners until it is part of the group. So no warm-up can be placed on it by this derivation, and none is discarded.

review_comments.body: This is already reworded in 4d188e7261: the javadoc now states the contract for implementations (must not newly place a warm-up task on a member that is not supported) and that the coordinator reconciles towards the target assignment if it does.
Fixed in 82dfbcc351 (that was also what failed spotless in CI).

Return an immutable map here. This map is passed to the configured refiner and then the same instance is used by the coordinator's invariant check. A faulty refiner can mutate an unsupported member to `SUPPORTED` before returning an invalid warm-up placement, causing `membersWithUnsupportedWarmupTasks` to accept exactly the placement the guard is intended to reject. The other coordinator-owned refiner inputs are exposed as immutable maps, so copying this snapshot also makes the contract consistent.
Fixed in 7368ea6f20: `warmupSupport()` returns an unmodifiable snapshot, with a test that it cannot be modified.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21111 [1/N]: Tell the refiner which members may be given a warm-up task

A warm-up task is only useful if the coordinator can observe how far its
holder has restored it, and members that speak version 0 of the streams
heartbeat never report that progress. Before the refiner can treat such
members differently, the coordinator has to know which version each member
speaks.

The coordinator now records the version of every member's last heartbeat
as transient state of the streams group, with the same lifecycle as the
reported task offsets: written in the heartbeat path, dropped when the
member is removed, and not known again after a coordinator failover until
the member heartbeats. From it, the refiner is handed one fact per member,
whether warm-up tasks are supported, not supported, or unknown. Members the
coordinator has not heard from since it loaded the group are unknown rather
than assumed to be new clients.

The refiner ignores the new input for now. The coordinator additionally
guards the invariant that a warm-up task never reaches a member that is not
known to support them: if an intermediate assignment violates it, the
coordinator logs an error and reconciles towards the target assignment
instead, which revokes the warm-up tasks, like it already does for an
intermediate assignment that loses an active task.

commit.message:
Document the warm-up support contract and test the backstop's kept warm-up rule

The javadoc of the refiner now states what an implementation must do with the support of a member, instead of describing what the refiner does. The rule that a member of unknown version, or a sibling in its process, may keep a warm-up task it already holds is covered by direct tests, next to the rule that a task newly placed on a member that is not supported is rejected.

Build the index of held warm-up tasks only when a member of unknown version needs it

The coordinator checks the refined assignment on every heartbeat of a group that is not reconciling. In the common case no member holds a warm-up task, so the check now returns without indexing the warm-up tasks of all members.

commit.message:
Store the warm-up support per member and drop the check of the refined assignment

The coordinator keeps the warm-up support derived from the heartbeat version, instead of the version itself, and hands the refiner an immutable view of it, so no map is built per heartbeat. A member that has not heartbeated is missing from it, which stands for unknown. The refiner does not act on the support yet, so the coordinator does not check the refined assignment against it either.

commit.message:
Pass the heartbeat versions of the members to the refiner

The coordinator keeps the version of each member's last heartbeat and hands the refiner an immutable view of it. Which versions report task offsets, and so can be given a warm-up task, is for the refiner to decide, and the version may serve other decisions later. A member that has not heartbeated since the coordinator loaded the group is missing from the map. The refiner ignores the input for now.

timeline.message:
Store the warm-up support per member and drop the check of the refined assignment

The coordinator keeps the warm-up support derived from the heartbeat version, instead of the version itself, and hands the refiner an immutable view of it, so no map is built per heartbeat. A member that has not heartbeated is missing from it, which stands for unknown. The refiner does not act on the support yet, so the coordinator does not check the refined assignment against it either.

Pass the heartbeat versions of the members to the refiner

The coordinator keeps the version of each member's last heartbeat and hands the refiner an immutable view of it. Which versions report task offsets, and so can be given a warm-up task, is for the refiner to decide, and the version may serve other decisions later. A member that has not heartbeated since the coordinator loaded the group is missing from the map. The refiner ignores the input for now.

issue.title: KAFKA-21111 [2/N]: Grant tasks at once to members that cannot be warmed up

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
This is the second change of the series that makes the warm-up task
refiner (KAFKA-20665) compatible with clients that speak version 0 of
the streams group heartbeat (see KAFKA-21111), on top of #23761.

A warm-up task can only complete a migration if the coordinator observes
the target owner restoring it, which a member that heartbeats with
version 0 never allows, as it does not report task offsets. When the
target assignment moves a stateful task to such a member, the refiner no
longer stages the migration. It lets the target assignment through for
that task, so the current owner revokes it and the target owner takes it
over, as it would without a refiner.

The check sits after the readiness check, so that a move between two
members of one process still happens inside the instance, and before the
analysis of the incumbent and of the copies, so that a caught-up copy on
another process is not promoted as a temporary owner. That detour would
only postpone the same cold grant and add a second hand-over. The
version of the current owner is irrelevant: a member that processes a
task is hot by definition, and keeps it while a target owner that can be
warmed up restores it. If the target owner already holds a standby task
of the task, the client recycles it into the active task, so the grant
is warm in the common case, even though the coordinator cannot see that.

The refiner is not the default yet, so this change is not live. The
tests cover the grant, the missing detour through a caught-up copy, and
a current owner of version 0 that keeps its task.

Reviewers: Bill Bejeck <bbejeck@apache.org>
